# Results numbers, and where each one comes from

**Generated by `figures/scripts/audit_numbers.py`. Do not edit by hand.**

Every value below is read from a `benchmark.csv` at run time. The
script then scans `sections/02-results.tex` and reports any decimal in
the prose that it cannot account for.

Columns: donor recovery and study mixing are **lower is better**;
cross-donor phase, cell family and disease are **higher is better**.

**Deltas against BASE**, for the claims that are stated as changes:

| arm | Δ family | Δ phase | Δ cell type | Δ disease | Δ donor | Δ mixing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| -phase head | -0.0026 | -0.2534 | -0.0428 | -0.0194 | -0.1434 | -0.1090 |
| -ECS | +0.0017 | +0.0051 | +0.0030 | +0.0274 | +0.0332 | +0.0727 |

| random groups | -0.0214 | -0.0566 | -0.0075 | -0.0666 | +0.0135 | +0.0088 |

**D1, recomputed.** Cross-donor values are already chance-corrected, so the phase margin splits as a ratio of the two excesses, not as a difference from a chance rate:

- base 0.7346, head removed 0.4812
- **65.5%** of the chance-corrected signal survives removing the head, so the head accounts for **34.5%** and the architecture for the rest.

The superseded figure was 30.5% surviving and 69.5% from the head, from (0.4812 - 0.370)/(0.7346 - 0.370). That subtracted chance from numbers chance had already been taken out of. 0.370 is the chance rate of a different measurement, the plain whole-corpus phase grouping in `grouped_agreement.csv`.

**The comparator for a cross-donor value is its own permutation null**, carried in the benchmark `note` column as `null95`: 0.18 for menstrual phase, 0.06 for cell family, 0.12 for grade, 0.42 for stage. Stage's 0.1313 sits below its own null95, which is why its p is 0.303.

## D2 and A7 — reconstruction, from the training metrics

`val_nb` and `train_nb` are mean negative-binomial loss per cell;
**lower is better**. The reported checkpoint is `argmin val_nb`,
which reproduces ABLATIONS.md's `best ep` column for every arm.

| arm | epochs | best ep | train_nb @best | val_nb @best | train_nb @last | val_nb @last | source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BASE** | 10 | 4 | 0.3785 | 0.4024 | 0.3762 | 0.4100 | `Outputs/p_series/p1_dab168_kl1/metrics.csv` |
| -phase head | 8 | 0 | 0.4140 | 0.4083 | 0.3772 | 0.4256 | `Outputs/a_series/a1_nophase/metrics.csv` |
| -ECS | 10 | 4 | 0.3789 | 0.4004 | 0.3761 | 0.4146 | `Outputs/a_series/a1_noecs/metrics.csv` |
| -statistics | 10 | 4 | 0.3791 | 0.3979 | 0.3760 | 0.4043 | `Outputs/a_series/a1_clsonly/metrics.csv` |
| -sentinel | 11 | 5 | 0.3777 | 0.4005 | 0.3758 | 0.4164 | `Outputs/a_series/a1_nodns/metrics.csv` |
| random groups | 18 | 12 | 0.3756 | 0.3911 | 0.3748 | 0.3919 | `Outputs/a_series/a1_randgroups/metrics.csv` |

**D2 reads down the `-phase head` row, not across to BASE.** Without the
head, `val_nb` is best at **epoch 0** and worsens monotonically from
epoch 1 while `train_nb` keeps falling — the held-out split is paid for
the training split from the first epoch onward. BASE's `val_nb`
improves to epoch 4 before it turns. Both trajectories are in the
table above; quoting 0.4083 as a BASE value would be wrong, it is the
`-phase head` arm's best.

**A7's study-mean reference (0.4315) is not in any file read here.**
It is a computed baseline, not a logged metric, and must be
re-derived from the code that produced it before it becomes prose.

| marecko_2024 | 0.5069 | 0.5057 | **0.8321** | 0.5697 | immune |

**Where the maximum sits, per arm:**

- **duempelmann_2026** — **not stable**: `p1_dab168_kl1` → immune, `p1_dab168_kl30` → endothelial. Range across both arms 0.1908 to 0.2892.
- **marecko_2024** — **immune** in every arm. Range across both arms 0.4276 to 0.8321.

C4 is the marecko immune cell, and it is the maximum in both arms at a
magnitude no other stratum reaches. C5 is duempelmann, where the
displacement is roughly a third of marecko's **and** the leading family
is not the same in the two arms — so the non-replication is both in
magnitude and in ordering, and prose may say so.

`reference_scales.csv` in the same folders carries the whole-corpus
cell-family distances that these are read against.

| cross-donor | cell family | 630,689 | 0.9807 | p=0.005; floor=0.000; null95=0.05; 66 kept; 118 donors |
| cross-donor | menstrual phase | 723,599 | 0.6796 | p=0.005; floor=0.000; null95=-0.00; 64 kept; 142 donors |
| cross-donor | severity (study vocabularies) | 631,090 | 0.2655 | p=0.005; floor=0.000; null95=0.01; 67 kept; 118 donors |
| cross-donor | EndometriosisGrade | 465,391 | 0.0263 | p=0.408; floor=0.000; null95=0.08; 75 kept; 60 donors |
| cross-donor | Endometriosis_stage | 164,474 | 0.3320 | p=0.005; floor=0.000; null95=0.03; 41 kept; 58 donors |

**The same-donor chance rate is 0.0060** over 269 donors (`sum n_d(n_d-1) / N(N-1)`), against an observed 0.327 of a cell's hundred nearest neighbours — **54x enriched**. The 14x figure in the figure notes is a 60-donor single-cohort subsample and is not a corpus number.

**Stage splits between the two reads and this matters.** Whole-corpus cross-donor stage is +0.3320 at p = 0.005, held-out +0.1313 at p = 0.3035. Any prose saying stage carries nothing *anywhere* contradicts the first figure.

**The best-of-sixteen caveat.** `linear-corr` takes the largest |r| over the latent's sixteen dimensions, so the negative controls do not sit near zero: 0.3396 for mitochondrial fraction against 0.4725 for serum progesterone. Quote the controls alongside.

Every `circular-linear` row is `nan`, so **no claim about the circular branch is available** from this file.

Donor agreement itself is **0.3270** (excess 0.3229 inverted through chance 0.0060), which is **54.5x** the chance rate.

## Numbers in the prose that this script cannot account for

None. Every decimal in the Results prose matches a value re-derived above, or is a chance rate carried in the benchmark's own `note` column.

## How the field table is sourced

Eight of the ten methods were already scored correctly. Nothing needed
re-running; what was wrong was which file each row was read from.

**The corpus is identical across every source in the manifest**, verified
from the runs' own logs: 416,256 held-out cells, with 176,803 cells
labelled for cell family, 224,211 for menstrual phase and 108,288 for cell
cycle phase. The reported arm and all four `fm_*` runs agree on all three.

**The four `fm_*` runs are one baseline pass.** `pca`, `scvi` and
`scanvi` hold bit-identical values and cell counts in all four files, so
those jobs scored the baselines once and added one pretrained model each.
Any one of the four is the source for the shared rows.

**ELAJ's row is unaffected by the baselines' gene axis.** It reads the
vocabulary its checkpoint was trained against whatever the baselines are
given, on the same cells, so its row from the narrow run stands beside the
wide baselines. That is why the wrapper documents `--no-elaj` for a wide
pass: re-embedding would reproduce the same row.

**The two gene policies are a choice, not a conflict.** `pca`, `scvi` and
`scanvi` were scored twice, on 15,496 genes in the reported arm and on
30,962 in the `fm_*` runs. Baselines are reported on the full axis, so the
wide rows are used and the narrow ones are discarded. Both are valid; only
one answers this paper's question.

**Differing `n_cells` per method is coverage, not a fault.** Cross-donor
agreement is measured only on cells with at least one cross-donor
neighbour, and that count is a property of the embedding.

**`r8_all` is the one genuine fault**, and it costs exactly two rows.
